necessary_context.content: x∈R^p, y∈R^q; Phi(x)=f(x,y*(x)), y*(x)=argmin_y g(x,y). Main Eq. (1) uses jointly continuously differentiable f,g. Assumption 1: g(x,·) is mu-strongly convex, and Phi is nonconvex in x. For arbitrary z=(x,y),z', Assumption 2 requires f to be M-Lipschitz and grad f and grad g to be L-Lipschitz; Assumption 3 requires g_xy to be tau-Lipschitz and g_yy to be rho-Lipschitz. A finite convergence bound also requires finite Phi(x0)−inf_x Phi(x).
necessary_context.locator: Main PDF p.1 Eq. (1); p.5 Assumptions 1–3; p.6 Theorem 1
necessary_context.name: Problem and deterministic assumptions

necessary_context.content: Definition 1 uses E||grad Phi(xbar)||^2≤epsilon rather than epsilon^2. Definition 2 counts each partial gradient, Jacobian-vector product, and Hessian-vector product separately. Supplement p.7 reports Gc(f)=2K, Gc(g)=KD, JV=K, HV=KN; these are the authors' counts for the selected AID-BiO algorithm, not unrestricted Oracle Complexity or a lower bound.

necessary_context.content: The denominator in the condition on D in Supplement PDF p.5 Eq. (21) is printed as log(1/(1−alpha)), whereas the GD contraction in its Proof is (1−alpha mu)^D. Eq. (30) is an additional absorption condition and cannot replace the condition required by Lemma 4. Only the issue in the original source is recorded here; no corrected Theorem is submitted.
